faq.q: Which cuisine has the most Michelin recognition?
faq.a: Fine Dining & International ranks first for star density: 22 of its 25 listed restaurants hold stars, led by three-star Sühring. Thai Cuisine follows with 20 stars across a much larger list of 60 restaurants.

faq.q: Is Thai food or fine dining better rewarded?
faq.a: They win on different measures. Fine Dining leads on the ratio of stars to restaurants, but Thai Cuisine has the deepest list at 60 spots, split between 20 starred restaurants and 40 Bib Gourmands, making it the easiest category to eat well in at any budget.

faq.q: Which category is the best value?
faq.a: Noodles and Street Food are the value plays. All 21 Noodle spots are Bib Gourmands, led by Gim Nguan Noodle, and all 14 Street Food entries are Bib too, led by A Pong Mae Sunee. Low prices with a Michelin nod attached.

faq.q: Why does Southern Thai rank so high with few restaurants?
faq.a: Southern Thai lists 22 restaurants with just one star, but that star is Sorn, the only three-star Southern Thai restaurant in the country. The other 21 are Bib Gourmands, giving the category both a towering peak and plenty of affordable eats.

faq.q: How did we rank these categories?
faq.a: We weight by star level first, then total count. A three-star counts more than a two-star, which counts more than a one-star, so star-dense categories rise to the top and Bib-heavy categories follow. A lower rank does not mean the food is any less delicious.
